topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: I stood there, breath caught in my throat, staring at the empty space where my tree once stood. It was more than just a tree; it was my childhood, my solace, my witness. Every leaf, every branch held whispers of my laughter and tears. Now, it’s just a stump, a cruel reminder of what’s gone. The air feels colder, the world a little more barren. I can’t wrap my head around it. Who would do this? Why? The ground beneath me seems unsteady, and the silence around me is deafening. I don’t know how to fill this void, how to move on from this emptiness.
